## 1. Scope of Application (Geltungsbereich)

1.1 These General Terms and Conditions (the "Terms" or "**AGB**") apply to all contracts, orders, deliveries and services between Auterion GmbH, Centa-Hafenbraedl-Strasse 61, 81249 Munich, Germany ("**Auterion**") and its customers, buyers, licensees, OEM partners, resellers or other contractual partners (each a "**Customer**") relating to Auterion Hardware, Auterion Software, Auterion Suite, professional services, OEM partnerships and related products or services.
1.2 These Terms apply exclusively. Deviating, conflicting or supplementary terms and conditions of the Customer do not become part of the contract, even if Auterion accepts an order, provides delivery or performance, grants access, activates a license key or does not expressly object to such terms. Any acceptance by Auterion is expressly conditional on the Customer accepting these Terms.
1.3 These Terms apply only to entrepreneurs (Unternehmer) within the meaning of § 14 BGB, legal entities under public law and special funds under public law. Auterion does not contract on the basis of these Terms with consumers (Verbraucher).
1.4 Individual agreements expressly agreed with the Customer in writing or in text form in an individual contract, order confirmation, statement of work or framework agreement take precedence over these Terms. In case of conflict, the following order applies: (a) an individually negotiated written agreement signed or confirmed by Auterion; (b) Auterion's order confirmation; (c) these Terms; (d) specifications expressly incorporated by Auterion; and (e) the Customer's order only to the extent expressly accepted by Auterion.
1.5 Legally relevant declarations and notices by the Customer, including notices of defects, deadline settings, withdrawal, reduction, termination, reminders and notices of set-off or retention, must be made at least in text form (§ 126b BGB), unless mandatory law requires a stricter form. Section 22 applies to notices.
1.6 Auterion may update these Terms for future contracts at any time. Amendments affecting an existing continuing obligation require the Customer's express consent in text form. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Auterion may make changes without such consent where required by a change in applicable law, a binding governmental or court order, or to address a material security vulnerability, provided that the change is limited to what is necessary, does not alter the essential contractual performance or price to the Customer's detriment, and is notified in text form with reasonable advance notice where practicable. If a proposed change would otherwise materially disadvantage the Customer, Auterion will offer the Customer a reasonable right to terminate the affected continuing obligation before the change takes effect, unless the change is legally mandatory and continuation on the existing terms is not permitted.
## 2. Definitions

2.1 "**Auterion Hardware**" or "**Products**" means all hardware products, reference designs, boards, devices, components, accessories and related physical items supplied by Auterion, including Skynode, Skynav and any successor products.
2.2 "**Auterion Software**" or "**Software**" means object code versions of Auterion software, including AuterionOS, PX4-based flight control software, Auterion Enterprise PX4, Auterion Mission Control, QGC Gov, SDKs, APIs, updates, maintenance releases, documentation and related components, regardless of delivery mechanism.
2.3 "**Auterion Suite**" means Auterion's SaaS, cloud, fleet-management, OTA-update, dashboard, API, telemetry, support, analytics and related online services.
2.4 "**Auterion Properties**" means Auterion Hardware, Software, Auterion Suite, specifications, documentation, APIs, source code (if any), reference designs, marks, confidential information, systems, data derived from operation or monitoring of Auterion Suite, Resultant Data, and all other technologies, materials and information provided or made available by Auterion.
2.5 "**Integrated Product**" means any unmanned aerial vehicle, autonomous system, payload, robot, ground station or other product incorporating, bundling, connecting to or otherwise using Auterion Properties.
2.6 "**OEM Partner**" means a Customer authorized by Auterion in an individual agreement to integrate Auterion Properties into Integrated Products for distribution to end users.
2.7 "**Customer Information**" means information relating to a Customer, end user, Authorized User, Integrated Product, license, activation, serial number, transaction, support event, telemetry event, usage statistic, registration or EULA acceptance.
2.8 "**EULA**" means Auterion's then-current end-user license agreement for the Software or Auterion Suite, as made available by Auterion from time to time.
2.8a “Authorized Users” means the Customer’s employees, contractors or agents who are individually authorized by the Customer to access Auterion Suite and who have accepted applicable use terms.
2.9 "**Specifications**" means the technical documentation, data sheets and functional descriptions expressly issued by Auterion for the relevant Auterion Property. Specifications do not include public advertising, general marketing statements, roadmaps, forecasts or non-binding product descriptions.

2.10 "**Regulated Items**" means Auterion Properties, Integrated Products, technology, technical data, software, source code, documentation and services that may be subject to export control, sanctions, customs, defense, dual-use, anti-boycott, anti-corruption, procurement or end-use restrictions.
2.11 "**Resultant Data**" means data and information related to use, performance, security, diagnostics, telemetry, compatibility and operation of Auterion Properties that Auterion uses in aggregated, anonymized or otherwise non-personal form for analytics, security, product improvement, support, benchmarking, statistics, machine-learning, service operation or business purposes.
2.12 "**Business Day**" means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday in Munich, Germany.
## 3. Conclusion of Contract and Order of Precedence ()

3.1 Auterion's offers, price lists, quotations, product descriptions, online information, Vertragforecasts, sschlusdelivery s estimates and other documents are non-binding invitations to submit an order unless expressly designated by Auterion as binding.
3.2 A Customer order constitutes a binding offer. Auterion may accept the offer within fourteen (14) calendar days after receipt, unless a different period is stated by Auterion. Acceptance may occur by written or text-form order confirmation, delivery, activation, provision of access, or commencement of performance.
3.3 Auterion may reject orders, in whole or in part, without stating reasons, including for credit, compliance, supply, export-control, sanctions, capacity, technical, certification or business reasons. Any consideration already received for a rejected order will be refunded without interest, unless set-off is permitted.
3.4 The content of the contract is determined by Auterion's order confirmation. The Customer must review the order confirmation promptly and notify Auterion of any discrepancy without undue delay. Silence does not constitute acceptance, except where and to the extent this follows from applicable statutory law or the principles governing commercial letters of confirmation (kaufmaennisches Bestaetigungsschreiben).
3.5 Auterion may make acceptance, delivery, license activation or performance conditional on advance payment, credit approval, export-control clearance, end-use documentation, receipt of required technical information, or other reasonable conditions.
## 4. Hardware Sales (Lieferung von Hardware)

### 4.1 Delivery, dispatch and transfer of risk

4.1.1 Unless expressly agreed otherwise in the individual contract, deliveries are made FCA Auterion's German dispatch facility or another dispatch point designated by Auterion (Incoterms 2020). If the parties validly agree Ex Works (Incoterms 2020), the Customer is responsible for loading, export, customs and transport to the maximum extent permitted by law.
4.1.2 Where delivery is agreed FCA, risk passes in accordance with the FCA rule at the named place. In other cases in which Products are shipped at the Customer's request, risk passes upon handover to the carrier, freight forwarder or other person designated to perform shipment in accordance with Section 447 BGB, unless otherwise individually agreed. If the Customer is in default of acceptance, risk passes when the Products are ready for dispatch and Auterion has notified the Customer thereof.
4.1.3 Delivery dates are non-binding estimates unless expressly confirmed by Auterion as fixed dates in writing. No fixed-date transaction (Fixgeschaeft) exists unless Auterion expressly confirms this in writing using that term.
4.1.4 Partial deliveries and partial invoices are permitted if reasonable for the Customer, in particular if the partial delivery is usable for the contractual purpose, delivery of the remainder is ensured, or Auterion has a legitimate interest in partial delivery.
4.1.5 Delivery periods are extended for the duration of events outside Auterion's reasonable control plus a reasonable restart period. A delay or failure by a supplier qualifies only if Auterion concluded a congruent covering transaction in due time, the supplier's failure was not caused by Auterion, and substitute procurement could not reasonably be obtained. Auterion will notify the Customer without undue delay of a material impediment and use reasonable efforts to mitigate its effects. If the impediment continues for more than three (3) months, either party may terminate the unperformed part of the affected order; Auterion will refund payments received for the terminated, unperformed part.
4.1.6 If Auterion is in default, the Customer may withdraw only after setting a reasonable grace period taking account of the circumstances of the individual case. Statutory cases in which a grace period is dispensable remain unaffected. Claims for damages due to delay are governed by Section 12.
4.1.7 If the Customer fails to accept Products, provide shipping instructions, obtain approvals, or pay amounts due, Auterion may store the Products at the Customer's risk and expense, invoice them, suspend further performance, cancel affected orders, and claim damages.

## 5. Software Licensing () Softwarelizenz

5.1 Subject to full and timely payment and ongoing compliance with the contract, Auterion grants the Customer a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable and non-sublicensable license during the agreed term and territory to use the Software in object code form solely with authorized Auterion Hardware and solely for the purposes expressly agreed in the individual contract. The license may be suspended or terminated only in accordance with Sections 5.7 and 17.
5.2 For non-OEM Customers, the license is limited to internal business use. For OEM Partners, the license is limited to integration into Integrated Products and distribution only as expressly permitted by Section 8 and the individual agreement. No standalone distribution of Software, source code, APIs, reference designs or documentation is permitted.
5.3 The Software is licensed, not sold. Auterion and its licensors retain all rights, title and interest in the Software, documentation, specifications, updates, maintenance releases, derivative works and all intellectual property rights.
5.4 The Customer may not copy, modify, translate, adapt, decompile, disassemble, reverse engineer, decode, circumvent technical protection, bypass license controls or attempt to derive source code, except as expressly permitted by the contract or by mandatory law, in particular Sections 69d and 69e UrhG. To the extent the Customer relies on Section 69e UrhG, it must first request the information necessary to achieve interoperability from Auterion and allow Auterion a reasonable period to provide it on reasonable terms.
5.5 The Customer may not use Auterion Properties for benchmarking, competitive analysis, training competing systems, developing competing products or services, vulnerability publication, security testing beyond agreed responsible-disclosure processes, or any use outside the agreed purpose without Auterion's prior written consent.
5.6 Any transfer of Software is permitted only together with the authorized hardware on which it is installed, only if the Customer permanently ceases use and deletes all copies, and only if the transferee validly accepts Auterion's applicable license terms. Mandatory exhaustion rules remain unaffected.
5.7 Auterion may use technical measures to activate, manage, monitor and secure licenses and access. Auterion may suspend or disable a license or access only to the extent reasonably necessary and proportionate to comply with law, address a material security risk, prevent material non-payment or remedy a material breach. Where practicable, Auterion will give reasonable prior notice and an opportunity to cure; immediate action is permitted where required by law or to address an urgent security or safety risk. Such measures will not intentionally interfere with an active flight or operation or create an avoidable safety risk.
## 6. Updates, Maintenance and Changes

6.1 Auterion provides updates, patches, maintenance releases or support only if expressly agreed or included in the applicable subscription or maintenance package and only while all fees are current and the Customer complies.
6.2 Updates and maintenance releases are deemed Software and are subject to these Terms. Auterion may modify, replace or update Auterion Properties, including APIs, features, hosting infrastructure, security controls and compatibility requirements, provided that the core contractual functionality is not materially reduced during a paid fixed term. If a change required by law, security, export control, supplier discontinuation, end-of-life or compelling technical reasons materially reduces that functionality, Auterion will give reasonable advance notice where practicable and offer

a reasonable alternative. If no reasonable alternative is available, the Customer may terminate the affected continuing service and receive a pro rata refund of prepaid fees for the period after termination.

6.3 Following reasonable notice and within a reasonable implementation period, the Customer must install security, safety, compliance and maintenance releases designated by Auterion as required, provided they are compatible with the supported environment described in the Specifications. Auterion is not responsible for defects, security incidents, incompatibilities or losses to the extent caused by the Customer's failure to implement such releases.
6.4 Auterion has no maintenance, warranty or support obligation for Software modified without authorization, used with unsupported hardware/software, used outside Specifications, used after end-of-life, or affected by Customer systems, third-party materials, accident, misuse or unauthorized repair.
6.5 New versions, feature upgrades, premium modules and professional services are not included unless expressly agreed and may be subject to additional fees and terms.
## 7. SaaS / Auterion Suite

7.1 If Auterion Suite access is provided, Auterion grants the Customer a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable and revocable right during the agreed term to access and use Auterion Suite via the internet solely for the agreed business purpose and solely through Authorized Users.
7.2 The Customer is responsible for its users, credentials, systems, internet connectivity, equipment, configurations, uploaded data, instructions, results and decisions based on use of Auterion Suite. All acts and omissions of Authorized Users are deemed acts and omissions of the Customer.
7.3 Auterion will use commercially reasonable efforts to make Auterion Suite available, subject to scheduled maintenance, emergency maintenance, third-party-provider issues, force majeure, security incidents, export-control or sanctions requirements and other circumstances outside Auterion's reasonable control. Any binding service levels apply only if expressly agreed in an SLA.
7.4 Auterion may suspend or restrict affected access to the extent reasonably necessary if Auterion reasonably believes that: (a) the Customer or an Authorized User is in material breach; (b) access creates a material security, legal, export-control, sanctions, data-protection, IP or operational risk; (c) payment is overdue; (d) a governmental or judicial request requires it; (e) use materially exceeds the agreed scope or technical limits; or (f) the contract expires or terminates. Where the issue is remediable, Auterion will provide prior notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure unless urgent action is required. Any measure must be proportionate in scope and duration. Termination is governed by Section 17.
7.5 The Customer must not upload unlawful, infringing, harmful, classified, export-restricted, malicious or unauthorized data or code to Auterion Suite and must maintain appropriate technical and organizational safeguards for Customer systems and credentials.
## 8. OEM Partner Terms

8.1 An OEM Partner receives distribution rights only if expressly designated by Auterion in an individual agreement. The rights are limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable, territory-limited and term-limited, and may be suspended or terminated for material breach in accordance with Section 17.
8.2 The OEM Partner may integrate Auterion Properties into Integrated Products and distribute Integrated Products only in the agreed territory, only to lawful customers and end users, and only with the Software in object code form as an integral part of the Integrated Product under the EULA. Standalone sale, resale, download, access, sublicensing or distribution of Auterion Properties is prohibited.
8.3 The OEM Partner is responsible for designing, configuring, assembling, manufacturing, testing, certifying, marketing, packaging, shipping, supporting and recalling Integrated Products and for ensuring that Integrated Products comply with all applicable laws, aviation rules, CE/UKCA or other conformity requirements, radio, cybersecurity, product safety, product liability, procurement, end-use, export-control and sanctions requirements. This allocation is without prejudice to any mandatory statutory obligations of Auterion and to Auterion's responsibility for defects in Auterion Properties under Sections 11 and 12.
8.4 Before commercial release, the OEM Partner must conduct all integration, safety, security, functional and compatibility testing reasonably necessary to verify that the Integrated Product operates with Auterion Properties in accordance with the agreed Specifications. Auterion may observe or participate in testing and may require evidence of testing.
8.5 Auterion may establish certification, quality, compatibility and brand requirements. The OEM Partner must obtain and maintain all required certifications and must not market or distribute Integrated Products that fail, lose or have not received required certification. Auterion is not obligated to certify any product that does not meet Auterion standards.
8.6 The OEM Partner must implement a process reasonably designed to ensure that end users validly accept the version of the EULA made available by Auterion before first use of the Software or Auterion Suite and must maintain evidence of such acceptance. Later EULA amendments apply to an end user only if validly incorporated under applicable law. The OEM Partner must not make representations, warranties, guarantees, claims, indemnities or commitments on Auterion's behalf or inconsistent with Auterion documentation.

8.7 Unless expressly agreed otherwise, the OEM Partner is solely responsible for first-line and second-line support to its customers and end users. The OEM Partner must direct customers to contact the OEM Partner, not Auterion, for support relating to Integrated Products. The foregoing does not relieve the OEM Partner of its obligations to (a) notify Auterion of potential defects in Auterion Properties without undue delay in accordance with Section 4.2, (b) immediately escalate to Auterion any complaint, incident or report relating to personal injury, property damage, flight safety, product safety or potential regulatory reporting obligations, and (c) cease support activities where continuing them would breach applicable export control, sanctions or end-use restrictions under Section 16. ## 9. Trademark License and Publicity

9.1 Subject to compliance, Auterion grants the Customer or OEM Partner a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable, royalty-free license during the term to use Auterion marks solely as expressly approved by Auterion and solely to market approved Integrated Products.
9.2 All use of Auterion marks must comply with Auterion brand guidelines and quality-control requirements. Auterion may require prior approval of mark placement, marketing materials, packaging, websites, press releases and public announcements.
9.3 All goodwill arising from use of Auterion marks inures exclusively to Auterion. The Customer must not challenge, register, use or assist others in using any mark, domain, company name or identifier confusingly similar to Auterion marks.
9.4 No party may issue press releases or public announcements referring to the other party or the contract without the other party's prior written consent, except as mandatory law or stock-exchange rules require.
## 10. Prices, Taxes and Payment

10.1 Prices are as individually agreed or, absent individual agreement, as set forth in Auterion's current price list at the time of acceptance. Price lists and quotations may be changed by Auterion for future orders unless expressly binding.
10.2 Unless expressly stated otherwise, all prices are net prices exclusive of VAT, customs, duties, levies, withholding taxes, bank charges, shipping, insurance, packaging beyond standard packaging, travel expenses and similar charges. Such amounts are borne by the Customer.
10.3 Unless otherwise agreed by Auterion in writing, payment for Hardware is due in full before delivery, activation or dispatch. Other invoices are due without deduction within fourteen (14) days of the invoice date. For future or outstanding performance, Auterion may require advance payment, suitable payment security, credit insurance or shorter payment terms if, after conclusion of the contract, objective circumstances arise that reasonably call the Customer's creditworthiness, compliance or payment performance into question. Section 321 BGB remains unaffected.
10.4 Payments must be made in euros to the account stated by Auterion, free of bank charges, set-off, deduction, recoupment or withholding. If withholding is required by law, the Customer must gross up the payment so that Auterion receives the amount it would have received absent withholding, unless prohibited by law.
10.5 If the Customer is in default, Auterion may charge default interest at nine (9) percentage points above the base rate (Section 288(2) BGB), claim the statutory lump sum under Section 288(5) BGB and recover further proven damages, including recoverable collection, legal and enforcement costs, subject to the Customer’s right to prove that Auterion suffered no damage or materially lower damage.
10.6 The Customer may set off only against undisputed claims or claims established by final judgment. This restriction does not apply to counterclaims arising from the same contractual relationship. Rights of retention may be asserted only if based on the same contractual relationship.
10.7 If payment is overdue, Auterion may suspend deliveries, services, support, license keys, SaaS access, updates and order processing, withhold performance, demand prepayment for all open orders, cancel orders and terminate for cause in accordance with Section 17.

<sub>of</sub> Auterion Hardware and Software is exclusively determined by the Specifications expressly incorporated by Auterion. Public statements, marketing materials, demonstrations, roadmaps, samples, prototypes, beta versions, development kits and advertising do not constitute agreed quality unless expressly confirmed by Auterion in writing.

11.2 Auterion does not warrant that Auterion Properties are suitable for a particular Customer purpose, compatible with unsupported systems, available without interruption, error-free, immune from cyber threats, compliant with laws outside the agreed market, or approved for any aviation, defense, government, safety-critical or end-use application, unless expressly agreed in writing.
11.3 If a defect exists at the time of transfer of risk and the Customer has complied with applicable inspection and notification duties, Auterion will provide subsequent performance (Nacherfuellung), at its statutory option, by repair or replacement delivery. Section 439 BGB and other mandatory statutory rights remain unaffected.
11.4 The Customer must provide reasonable cooperation, access, logs, data, returned products and test environments necessary for subsequent performance. Auterion may refuse subsequent performance to the extent legally permissible if it is impossible, disproportionate or if the Customer has not paid the due purchase price or fees in relation to the defect-free portion.
11.5 If subsequent performance fails, is refused or is unreasonable after a reasonable number of attempts, the Customer may reduce the price or withdraw from the affected contract in accordance with statutory law. Damages and reimbursement of futile expenditure are governed exclusively by Section 12.
11.6 Warranty rights are excluded to the extent a defect was caused by normal wear and tear, improper storage, transport after risk transfer, installation, operation, maintenance, calibration or handling, accident, environmental conditions, power supply, unauthorized repair, opening of seals or enclosures, modifications not approved by Auterion, use with non-approved hardware, software, operating systems, power modules or third-party components, failure to install required updates, Customer specifications or instructions, or use outside the Specifications.
11.7 Development products, prototypes, beta versions, evaluation licenses, samples, loaned equipment, no-cost products and pre-release features are provided "as is" and without warranty to the maximum extent permitted by law.
11.8 The limitation period for defect claims is twelve (12) months from delivery, transfer of risk, activation or acceptance, as applicable. This does not apply to claims based on injury to life, body or health, intentional or grossly negligent breach, fraudulent concealment, an expressly assumed guarantee, the German Product Liability Act, or where longer periods are mandatory, including under Sections 438(1) nos. 1 and 2, 445b and 478 BGB or Section 634a(1) no. 2 BGB, as applicable.
11.9 For SaaS and continuing services, Auterion's warranty is limited to reasonable efforts to restore agreed functionality within a reasonable time. The Customer's remedy for service defects is governed by the agreed SLA, if any, and otherwise by statutory law as limited in these Terms.
## 12. Liability () Haftung

12.1 Auterion is liable without limitation for damages arising from injury to life, body or health caused by intentional or negligent breach of duty by Auterion, its legal representatives or vicarious agents.
12.2 Auterion is liable without limitation for damages caused intentionally or by gross negligence, for fraudulent concealment of a defect, for guarantees expressly assumed by Auterion, and under the German Product Liability Act (Produkthaftungsgesetz).
12.3 In case of slight negligence, Auterion is liable only for breach of material contractual obligations (wesentliche Vertragspflichten/Kardinalpflichten). Such liability is limited to foreseeable, contract-typical damages. A material obligation is an obligation whose fulfilment is essential for proper contract performance and on whose compliance the Customer regularly relies and may rely.
12.4 Subject to Sections 12.1 and 12.2, liability under Section 12.3 is capped per damaging event at the higher of: (a) the net fees paid or payable by the Customer for the affected order or service during the twelve (12) months preceding the first event giving rise to liability; or (b) EUR 250,000. For Hardware-only orders, the amount under paragraph (a) is the net purchase price of the affected Products. If, due to the nature and scope of a particular contract, this cap does not reasonably reflect the foreseeable, contract-typical damage, liability remains limited to the amount of such foreseeable, contract-typical damage.
12.5 Auterion is not liable for a slightly negligent breach of non-material obligations. In cases governed by Section
12.3, lost profits, loss of revenue, loss of production or use, business interruption, loss of goodwill, indirect or consequential damages, frustrated savings and third-party procurement costs are excluded only to the extent they are not foreseeable and contract-typical. Liability for loss of data is limited to the reasonable cost of restoring the data from proper backups maintained by the Customer, unless data backup was itself owed by Auterion. Sections 12.1 and
12.2 remain unaffected.

## 13. Intellectual Property, Feedback and Resultant Data

13.1 Auterion and its licensors retain all right, title and interest in Auterion Properties, including all intellectual property rights, know-how, trade secrets, derivative works, improvements, modifications, feedback implementations, updates and related materials. No rights are granted except those expressly stated.
13.2 To the extent the Customer, with Auterion's authorization, creates a modification or derivative work specifically of an Auterion Property, the Customer assigns to Auterion all transferable intellectual property rights in that modification or derivative work and, where a right cannot be assigned, grants Auterion an exclusive, worldwide, perpetual, transferable, sublicensable and royalty-free right to use it for all known purposes. Feedback is licensed to Auterion on a non-exclusive basis on the same territorial, temporal, transfer and sublicensing terms. This Section does not transfer the Customer's pre-existing technology, general know-how, independently developed technology or rights in an Integrated Product other than the relevant modification or derivative work. Rights in commissioned developments and inventions must be addressed in the applicable statement of work. Mandatory moral rights and statutory remuneration rights remain unaffected.
13.3 Feedback, suggestions, ideas, requests, test results, comments and recommendations provided by the Customer may be used by Auterion without restriction or compensation, provided Auterion does not disclose the Customer's Confidential Information except as permitted.
13.4 Auterion may collect, generate and use Resultant Data for service operation, security, support, analytics, product improvement, benchmarking, statistics and R&D only in aggregated or effectively anonymized form so that neither the Customer, an individual, an Integrated Product nor a mission or operation is reasonably identifiable. Resultant Data does not include Customer content, Customer Confidential Information, classified information or export-controlled technical data, except to the extent separately agreed or strictly necessary to provide support, maintain security or comply with law. Personal data is processed only in accordance with applicable data-protection law and any applicable data processing agreement.
13.5 The Customer must promptly notify Auterion of any actual or suspected infringement, misappropriation, unauthorized access, misuse or challenge relating to Auterion Properties and must reasonably cooperate in protecting and enforcing Auterion rights.
